context: Operational server health dashboard — a data visualization tool showing 20 servers with CPU sparklines, bullet charts for memory, uptime bars, and KPI summary cards, all recoloring live as threshold sliders are adjusted.
first_impression: A genuinely polished, information-dense dashboard with deliberate design choices — colorblind-safe palette, multiple encoding types, and satisfying live-update interactivity — that reads as purposefully built rather than generated.
what_works: Deliberate use of Paul Tol's colorblind-safe palette (#228833/#CCBB44/#EE6677) instead of default D3 colors is a non-obvious, intentional choice that elevates the whole piece; the sparklines with inline threshold bands and the FLIP sort animation show real craft. Typography hierarchy is solid — uppercase letter-spaced headers, monospace tabular numbers, quieter status text.
what_doesnt: The Memory column truncates the GB labels in the rendered view ('9.6/16(' visible instead of full text), a concrete layout bug that undermines the bullet chart encoding. The 6px-tall uptime bars are barely visible at table row height, making that encoding nearly useless at a glance.
